claims.text: ``previously_passed`` is "this exact vendor+model+probe has an ``ok`` on record". That is what makes ``regressed`` mean "it used to work and now it does not" rather than "it is red", and it is why a lane that has never passed cannot page anyone: there is no evidence it ever could.
claims.why: In the code, previously_passed = bool(oks) and regressed = previously_passed and result.status in FAILING_STATUSES. This matches the claim: previously_passed is True only if there is at least one 'ok' in history, and regressed requires both previously_passed and a failing status. A lane that never passed would have previously_passed=False, so regressed=False.

claims.text: An ``unavailable`` result is NEVER a regression. We did not ask, so nothing regressed -- the bench being asleep is not the bench being broken.
claims.why: The code sets asked = [h for h in prior if h.get('status') != 'unavailable'] and later computes prior_pass_rate using len(oks)/len(asked). The status 'unavailable' is excluded from the denominator and not counted as a failure. Regressions are only determined by result.status in FAILING_STATUSES, and 'unavailable' is not in that set (as seen in _VERDICT where 'unavailable' is mapped to 'unavail' but not in FAILING_STATUSES). Additionally, the comment in render_table says 'unavailable is NOT failure'.

claims.text: ``previously_passed`` is "this exact vendor+model+probe has an ``ok`` on record".
claims.why: previously_passed = bool(oks) and oks is defined as [h for h in prior if h.get('status') == 'ok'], so it is True only if at least one prior record has status 'ok'.

claims.text: ``regressed`` mean "it used to work and now it does not"
claims.why: regressed = previously_passed and result.status in FAILING_STATUSES. The code requires a prior 'ok' and a current failing status, which matches 'used to work and now does not'.

claims.text: a lane that has never passed cannot page anyone: there is no evidence it ever could.
claims.why: If there are no 'ok' records, previously_passed is False, so regressed is False. The code does not define paging logic here, but the claim about regressed being false is correct. The paging behavior is elsewhere but the condition for regression is as stated.

claims.text: An ``unavailable`` result is NEVER a regression. We did not ask, so nothing regressed
claims.why: The code does not include 'unavailable' in FAILING_STATUSES (not defined here but referenced; the claim is about the logic in this function). The prior_pass_rate excludes 'unavailable' from the denominator, and regressed only checks result.status in FAILING_STATUSES, which does not include 'unavailable'. The comment in render_table also reinforces this.

claims.text: the bench being asleep is not the bench being broken
claims.why: This is a metaphor. The code does not reference 'bench' or 'asleep'. The claim is about interpretation, not a checkable code property.

observations.what: compare_to_history uses a trailing window of history entries, but the window is applied after filtering by vendor/model/probe, not before. This means if there are more than window entries, only the last window are used.
The rendering function render_table references r.failed_check and r.reason which are attributes of ProbeResult not defined in this chunk.
observations.where: render_table, line: detail = r.failed_check or r.reason

observations.what: render_table uses run.summary() which is a method on CanaryRun not defined in this chunk.
